title: Joe Root's Unbeaten 99 Steers England to Victory Over India in Cardiff, Sets Up Lord's Decider

body:
Key Takeaways
  • Joe Root scored an unbeaten 99, leading England to a four-wicket victory over India.
  • India collapsed from 104 for 1 to 233 all out, losing their last seven wickets for 55 runs.
  • Jofra Archer took 3 wickets for 47 runs, while Gus Atkinson achieved career-best figures of 3-50.
  • The series is now tied 1-1, setting up a decisive match at Lord's on Sunday.
  • India's captain Rohit Sharma faces scrutiny as younger players are considered for the World Cup.
Joe Root produced one of his finest one-day innings, scoring an unbeaten 99 off 133 balls, to steer England to a four-wicket victory over India in the second ODI at Cardiff on Wednesday. The result levels the three-match series at 1-1 and sets up a thrilling decider at Lord's on Sunday.

India's Collapse Proves Costly

India, the world's top-ranked ODI side, appeared well-placed at 104 for 1 before a dramatic collapse saw them lose their last seven wickets for just 55 runs. Shreyas Iyer top-scored for the visitors with 66, while Virat Kohli contributed an elegant 65 — his 132nd ODI innings of 50 or more — but the middle order crumbled spectacularly. Jofra Archer was the chief destroyer, finishing with figures of 3-47 including being on a hat-trick after dismissing Axar Patel and Shivam Dube in successive deliveries. Gus Atkinson complemented him superbly with career-best ODI figures of 3-50, as India were bowled out for 233 with six overs unused.

Root Anchors the Chase

England's reply began disastrously when Jasprit Bumrah dismissed Ben Duckett with the first ball of the innings, and Jacob Bethell followed quickly. Even captain Harry Brook and Jos Buttler fell to rash shots, leaving England in early trouble. But Root was the constant throughout, deflecting, grafting, and accumulating with the kind of patience and skill that has defined his career. He and Will Jacks put on 72 for the sixth wicket before Atkinson — who made a brisk 23 not out off 16 balls — helped Root see England home with 35 balls to spare. Root hit nine fours in what was his fifth consecutive ODI score above 50. He was stranded one short of a century, but getting England over the line was clearly the priority.

Diaspora Interest Peaks Ahead of Lord's

The series decider at Lord's on Sunday is expected to draw significant diaspora interest, with London's large Indian community typically turning the Home of Cricket into a sea of blue jerseys. The match will be pivotal for India's preparation ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa.
Root's Steady Performance
›Joe Root scored 99 off 133 balls.
›Hit 9 fours during his innings.
›Fifth consecutive ODI score above 50.
›Partnership of 72 runs with Will Jacks.
›England won with 35 balls to spare.
A notable subplot involves captain Rohit Sharma's future — reports suggest the BCCI may be looking at younger opening options including Yashasvi Jaiswal, Ruturaj Gaikwad, and Ishan Kishan for the World Cup, with the England tour seen as crucial for Rohit's continued selection. Jasprit Bumrah provided a bright note for India with an unbeaten 20 — his highest ODI score — showing the kind of lower-order resistance that will be needed if India are to bounce back at Lord's.
